implications.says: the sender was at the Leeds office at four, and Mrs. Holt was at the fête in Thornby from three until five: it was not she
Mr. Grove went to Leeds by the two o'clock train, and Mrs. Holt was not there: it was Mr. Grove
one key to the mill was drawn that evening, and it was Mr. Grove's: it was not Mrs. Holt who waited there
the telegram was his, naming the mill at ten, and he drew his key at half past nine: it was Mr. Grove who waited
